question: The average weight of A, B and C is 45 kg. If the average weight of A and B is 39 kg and that of B and C is 48 kg, then the weight of B (in kg) is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Weight of **B** = [Sum of (A + B) + Sum of (B + C)] − Sum of (A + B + C)

Weight of **B** = (2 × 39) + (2 × 48) − (3 × 45)

Weight of **B** = 78 + 96 − 135 = 174 − 135

Weight of **B** = 39 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 39 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average weight of **A, B, and C** = 45 kg

Average weight of **A and B** = 39 kg

Average weight of **B and C** = 48 kg

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6fce19ac9e08c7e35c84a01ead076d2dd57845b78c20fa6c9dd98fdf87cef24d.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Sum of values = **Average** × **Number of observations**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total weight of A + B + C = 3 × 45 = 135 kg

⇒ Total weight of A + B = 2 × 39 = 78 kg

⇒ Total weight of B + C = 2 × 48 = 96 kg

⇒ Sum of (A + B) and (B + C) = 78 + 96 = 174 kg

⇒ This sum can be written as: (A + B + C) + B = 174 kg

⇒ 135 + B = 174

⇒ B = 174 − 135

⇒ B = 39 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 39 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Definition of Average

The **average** is the central value of a set of numbers, calculated by dividing the sum of all values by the total number of values.

Overlap Principle

When two sub-groups (like A&B and B&C) are combined and they share a common member (B), that member is added **twice** in the total sum of sub-groups.

Deviation Method

Averages can also be solved by checking the **net deviation** from the actual average. Sum of deviations from the mean is always zero.</p
